description: Source record for Research Intelligence (Section 2, tasks 11-13, 16). Filed by the literature-researcher job (see agents/literature-researcher.md and literature.py). A search result is a lead, never evidence: only a retrieved ORIGINAL source with a locator and a content hash is a source record. Each record carries the one-line claim it supports (supports_claim) so the brief assembler can pin claims to sources; unpinned claims are dropped, never filed. stance marks whether the source supports or disputes supports_claim and feeds the contradiction check (mark_contested): opposing stances on the same claim mark it contested, never silently resolved. Model-written synthesis is UNIMPLEMENTED here; briefs are assembled deterministically from these records.

id.description: Stable source identifier within the lab, e.g. SRC-001. Claims cite this id to pin themselves to the record.

citation.description: Full bibliographic citation: authors, year, title, venue/container, persistent identifier (DOI/URL) where one exists.

retrieved_at.description: Retrieval date of the original source, ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp). When the source was actually fetched, not when it was published.

access_note.description: Licence / access note: licence terms (e.g. CC-BY, closed), access path (open-access, institutional, paywalled method), and any reuse constraint. A paywalled method is stated here, never hidden.

supports_claim.description: One-line claim this source actually shows, stated as what the source demonstrates (not as established fact). The brief assembler pins brief claims against this line.

locator.description: Locator inside the source: DOI, dataset row range, section/passage reference. A finding whose trail does not end at a locator is unfounded.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest (64 hex chars) of the retrieved original content. The hash is what makes the source checkable; a search result has no hash and stays a lead.

stance.description: Stance of this source toward supports_claim: 'supports' (default) or 'disputes'. Two sources with opposing stances on the same claim line mark the claim contested (literature.mark_contested); the conflict is flagged, never silently resolved.

title.description: Optional short title of the source for brief display. The citation remains the authoritative reference.
